summary: Master digital humanitarian aid strategies. Learn IASC guidelines, KoboToolbox, and data responsibility to lead high-impact crisis response. Enroll today.
lede: Digital Transformation in Humanitarian Aid helps professionals integrate digital technologies into humanitarian operations, improving the efficiency, reach, monitoring, and evaluation of crisis response. This course focuses on turning fragmented tools and data into a cohesive operational strategy while maintaining strong data ethics and operational resilience. Across five days, you will practise mobile data collection, automated reporting, Cash and Voucher Assistance technologies, secure data workflows, digital identity management, and humanitarian dashboards using KoboToolbox and Power BI. You will also explore predictive analytics and blockchain at an overview level, building the practical skills to translate field data into actionable insights under limited connectivity, shifting security conditions, and donor compliance requirements.
audienceIntro: This program is tailored for mid-to-senior level professionals responsible for the design and execution of humanitarian interventions in diverse global contexts.
audience: Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) Specialists using remote
modules: Humanitarian Digital Ecosystem and IASC Guidelines
Mobile Data Collection and Field Information Management
Digital Cash and Voucher Assistance (CVA) Systems
Data Responsibility and Protection Impact Assessments
Emerging Technologies and Predictive Humanitarian Action
Digital Strategy and Stakeholder Change Management
prerequisites: Participants should have at least 3 years of experience in humanitarian program management, monitoring and evaluation, or information management. A basic understanding of the humanitarian program cycle and familiarity with Microsoft Excel is required. No prior coding or programming experience is necessary, though familiarity with mobile data collection tools is an advantage.
